requestKey: Daily stretches for people who sit all day|sway.day|sample0

payload.text:
Here’s a simple, no‑equipment routine designed for people who sit a lot. Do a 60–90 second “desk reset” every 30–60 minutes, plus the 10-minute daily stretch flow once per day. Move slowly, breathe, and stop if you feel sharp pain or numbness.

Desk reset (60–90 seconds)
- Chest opener: Interlace fingers behind you (or hold chair back), straighten elbows, lift chest; 20–30 seconds.
- Chin tucks: Gently draw head straight back (give yourself a “double chin”); 8–10 slow reps.
- Standing backbend: Hands on hips, gently extend through upper/mid-back; 5–6 slow reps.
- Wrist relief: Extend one arm, pull fingers back for forearm stretch, then down; 15 seconds each position per side.

Daily stretch flow (about 10 minutes)
1) Neck and upper traps
- Side neck stretch: Ear toward shoulder, other hand gently anchors the chair; 30 seconds each side.
- Levator scap stretch: Turn nose toward armpit, gently nod down; 30 seconds each side.

2) Chest and upper back
- Doorway pec stretch: Elbow at shoulder height on doorframe, step through until you feel a chest stretch; 30–45 seconds each side.
- Thoracic extension over chair: Sit tall, hands behind head, lean upper back over chair back; 8–10 slow reps.
- Optional: Thread‑the‑needle on hands/knees for a gentle upper‑back twist; 6–8 reps each side.

3) Hips (the big one for sitters)
- Hip‑flexor lunge: Half‑kneeling, tuck pelvis (glute squeeze), shift forward slightly until you feel the front‑of‑hip stretch; 45–60 seconds each side.
- Figure‑4 glute stretch: Sit tall, ankle over opposite knee, hinge forward; 45–60 seconds each side.
- 90/90 hip rotations (floor or seated variation): Rotate knees side‑to‑side keeping spine tall; 6–8 reps each side.

4) Hamstrings and calves
- Hamstring hinge: Heel on floor or low step, knee soft, hinge from hips with flat back; 45–60 seconds each side.
- Calf wall stretch: Back leg straight, heel down; 30–45 seconds, then bend back knee to hit the deeper calf; 20–30 seconds each.

5) Spine decompression
- Cat–cow on hands/knees: 6–10 slow reps.
- Child’s pose or kneeling prayer stretch on desk: 30–45 seconds.

Form and pacing tips
- Intensity: Aim for a 3–4 out of 10 stretch sensation—no pain, no tingling.
- Breath: Inhale through the nose, exhale slowly; try a 4‑second inhale, 6‑second exhale.
- Progression: Add 5–10 seconds per stretch each week, or an extra set of reps for the mobility moves.

If you only have 5 minutes
- Doorway pec stretch: 1 minute total.
- Thoracic extension over chair: 1 minute.
- Hip‑flexor lunge: 1 minute each side.
- Figure‑4 glute stretch: 1 minute total (30s/side).

Helpful habits for sitters
- Stand or walk 2–5 minutes every 30–60 minutes.
- Keep screen at eye level, feet flat, hips and knees near 90°, and use the chair backrest.
- Get 5,000–8,000+ steps daily if you can.
